Mumbai Local Rush: Minister Urges Private Offices To Offer Flexible Work Hours Too
Pratap Sarnaik also said the state is in talks with Railways Ministry to convert all local trains into air-conditioned (AC) coaches while retaining the current fare structure.
In a significant move to reduce crowding in Mumbai’s overburdened local trains, Maharashtra Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik has announced a new measure allowing state government employees to start work 30 minutes later than usual. This initiative, aimed at easing congestion during peak hours, requires government staff to extend their working hours by half an hour to ensure no productivity loss.
Speaking to News18, Sarnaik emphasised that the decision is part of a broader strategy to address the city’s chronic transport woes. “To reduce the crowd during morning and evening peak hours in local trains, we have started this initiative for government employees. They can come half an hour late but must stay half an hour longer," he said.

The state government hopes this adjustment will act as a model and eventually encourage private offices to adopt similar staggered working hours. A study group is being formed to evaluate and recommend suitable time slots for private sector offices. Sarnaik appealed to private employers to cooperate in the interest of public safety. “They also have to understand that their employees travel in local trains. For their safety, they should change office timings," he said.
However, the government has no legal mandate to enforce these changes on private companies. “We can’t compel them or take legal action. We will write to them and try to convince them," Sarnaik clarified, suggesting a persuasive and cooperative approach rather than a regulatory one.
Mumbai’s local train network, often dubbed the city’s lifeline, carries over 70 lakh commuters daily. Rush hour crowding is a persistent concern, frequently leading to commuter injuries and even fatalities due to overcrowding and people falling off trains.
To further enhance commuter safety, Sarnaik revealed that the state is in talks with the Union Railways Ministry to convert all local trains into air-conditioned (AC) coaches while retaining the current fare structure. “We are in discussions to make all trains AC with the same rates, so that accidents due to open doors can be prevented," he said, referring to the safety benefit of closed-door AC coaches.
